A 29-year-old primigravid woman at 24 weeks' gestation comes to the physician for a routine prenatal
visit. She has had occasional tiredness and frequent urination throughout her pregnancy but has
otherwise been well. She has attended all scheduled prenatal visits up to this point. Her weight gain
has been normal. Medical history is unremarkable. Current medications are prenatal supplements. Vital
signs are within normal limits. Examination shows a fundal height consistent with a 24-week gestation.
Laboratory studies show: | Hemoglobin | 11.2 g/dL | | --- | --- | | Mean corpuscular volume | 81 μm3 | |
Leukocyte count | 10,500/mm3 | | Platelet count | 155,000/mm3 | | Serum | | | Creatinine | 0.4 mg/dL | |
Glucose | 102 mg/dL | Arterial blood gas analysis on room air shows: | pH | 7.44 | | --- | --- | | pO2 | 106
mm Hg | | pCO2 | 31 mm Hg | | HCO3- | 21 mEq/L | Results of an oral glucose tolerance test are within
the reference ranges. Ultrasonography shows the fetus in a transverse lie. Which of the following is the

most appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Serum iron studies (B) Order
complete blood count in 4 weeks (C) Perform amniocentesis (D) Urine culture (E) Schedule weekly
fetal monitoring (F) Schedule cesarean delivery (G) No further action is indicated (H) Initiate tocolytic
therapy (I) Initiate iron supplementation (J) Perform external cephalic version
 A. Schedule weekly fetal monitoring
